I have farmed here a long time, and with 60 mu plus well irrigation, I will keep the land arranged in the way that feels safest and most practical for my family. I will put the main land into wheat followed by summer maize, because that is the steadiest way for me to hold grain output and use the land fully. I will keep spring peanut on a good share of land because it fits my usual system, sells for cash, and is easier for me to manage than expanding cotton too much. I will still plant some cotton, but I will keep cotton area smaller because it takes more labor, and my household has some off-farm work, so I do not want to put too much land into a crop that needs more careful picking and management. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, and I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical rather than excessive, because I want steady output and lower risk, not the highest possible input bill.
